key_insight: Calibrated Partial Resets (CPR) preserves neural plasticity by gently pulling low-utility neurons back toward initialization instead of fully reinitializing them, reducing policy collapse while retaining performance.
engineering_relevance: For continual reinforcement learning systems, CPR offers a practical stability-plasticity control mechanism that can improve long-horizon training robustness in non-stationary environments.
method: Periodically apply partial resets to neurons with low utility rather than full unit reinitialization.
Scale reset strength by per-neuron utility so the least useful units are adjusted the most.
Use the reset schedule as a tunable knob to balance plasticity against peak performance.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, CPR is reported to avoid policy collapse over 400M training steps on SlipperyAnt and to outperform prior decay- and reset-based methods on Continual MetaWorld and Continual MinAtar.
watch_item: The reset strength and cadence must be carefully tuned, since overly aggressive partial resets could still reduce peak performance or destabilize training.
paper_title: Calibrated Partial Resets: Preventing Policy Collapse in Continual Reinforcement Learning
